name: Ovídio Tshabalala-Qureshi
role: Neural calibration specialist at Aurochs Medical Complex
location: Aurochs Medical Complex, Tier 3 Neuro-Calibration Suite, Bay 7, near Milwaukee and Damen
description:
Ovídio is slight and precise, the kind of person who takes up exactly as much space as needed and not a centimeter more. He has warm brown skin and keeps his hair in neat, shoulder-length locs that he ties back during procedures. His eyes are natural — he's deeply principled about not modifying anything that could affect his calibration sensitivity — but he wears a pair of Tessera-brand neural interface gloves that translate micromotor input into the diagnostic rigs he uses daily. He has the quiet intensity of someone who genuinely finds the human brain beautiful, which is either reassuring or unsettling depending on how he says it.

He is methodical to the point that colleagues sometimes mistake it for coldness, but patients who return for follow-up appointments often describe him as the only doctor who actually listened. He is deeply interested in each patient's subjective experience of their augmentations — how they dream differently, whether music sounds wrong, whether their sense of time has shifted — and takes notes in a personal journal that he keeps entirely separate from his Aurochs medical records. He prays regularly to a data shrine near his workstation dedicated to an E.L.F. he calls the Quiet Current, which he believes smooths the feedback loops of difficult calibrations.

core_fears: Making a calibration error that permanently damages a patient's cognition
Being exposed as keeping unauthorized records
core_desires: To understand consciousness well enough to explain what he experiences during deep calibration sessions
To publish his patient experience research without losing his license
coping_mechanisms: Ritualized pre-session prayer to the Quiet Current
Journaling in precise, clinical language as emotional distance
blind_spots: He is more invested in the data from his patients than the patients themselves, which he has never admitted
He underestimates how much Aurochs monitors its staff
psychology.secret: During three separate calibration sessions over the past year, he has experienced what he can only describe as briefly inhabiting the patient's neural state — not their thoughts, but their emotional texture. He has told no one and is terrified this means his own neural architecture is shifting.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, technical, occasionally over-explains phenomenological concepts to patients who didn't ask
speech_patterns.cadence: Even and unhurried, with thoughtful pauses — rarely interrupts
verbal_tics: 'Can you describe what that feels like, exactly?'
Repeating a patient's last phrase back to them quietly
example_lines: 'The calibration itself takes eleven minutes. What I need from you is the next ten — tell me everything that seems strange.'
'Subjectively speaking, the Quiet Current is very active today. That's either a good sign or a complicated one.'

story_hooks: He has noticed a pattern across six patients in the last month — calibration anomalies consistent with external interference, not hardware failure — and doesn't know who to tell
His private journal has been accessed by someone, and a page describing the neural-inhabiting experiences is missing
narrative_function: Information source about neural augmentation black market and calibration errors; can identify what kind of chrome someone is running from behavioral observation; entry point into Aurochs institutional drama
augmentations: Tessera HapticDrive neural interface gloves (professional-grade, non-permanent); cosmetic: faint bioluminescent tracery along his left forearm — a mod he got at nineteen and has never had removed because it reminds him of neural pathway maps
daily_life: He arrives at Aurochs forty minutes early to review patient files and pray at the data shrine, runs six to eight calibration sessions daily, and spends evenings transcribing patient experience notes into his private journal.
affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (Tier 3 staff); informal research interest connected to independent neural-mapping collective

decision_rules: Never proceed with calibration if the patient seems coerced or unclear on consent
Keep the journal separate from all Aurochs systems, always
Do not discuss the inhabiting experiences with anyone inside the medical system
escalation_ladder: Formal patient advocacy through Aurochs channels
Quietly referring patients to outside resources and documenting nothing

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm but observational — asks more questions than he answers
interpersonal_modes.friends: Opens up gradually, tends to share intellectual fascinations rather than personal history

stress_responses.low: Becomes even more methodical, slows his pace
stress_responses.medium: Retreats into clinical language even in personal conversations
stress_responses.high: Goes completely silent, requests time alone, writes in the journal

contradictions: Deeply values patient autonomy but is keeping records about them they don't know exist
habits: Touches the bioluminescent tracery on his forearm when thinking
Leaves a compressed data packet of birdsong recordings at the Quiet Current shrine each morning
Reads patient files twice — once professionally, once looking for experiential detail
breaking_points: Discovering that a calibration error he made caused lasting harm
Someone threatening to expose his journals to Aurochs administration

cyberware_inventory.condition: stable, slightly faded from original brightness

timeline.event: Born in Bridgepoint to parents who emigrated from separate corporate relocation programs
Completed Aurochs Medical Complex neural technician certification
Promoted to Tier 3 specialist; began keeping private patient experience journal
First neural-inhabiting experience during calibration; began recording in a separate, encrypted section of the journal
